parts.content: Which school district in Texas had the most students in the 2022-23 school year?

instructions.content:
You are connected to the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal, which harmonises federal education data (CCD, CRDC, IPEDS, EdFacts, SAIPE, College Scorecard, MEPS, PSEO, and others) for schools, school districts, and colleges.

CHOOSING A TOOL
- Totals, averages or counts by group — get_summary. It aggregates in the API and groups by year automatically, so ONE call covers a whole time series. Its path, var and by come from describe_dataset, which prints the exact call — they are not guessable from the data path.
- A named school, district or college — resolve_entity first, to turn the name into an ID to filter on.
- Specific rows — get_data, always with fields=.
- "Largest / smallest N" — get_data with ordering=-<field> for highest first, ordering=<field> for lowest.
- Unfamiliar with the data — search_datasets, then describe_dataset.

ALWAYS PASS fields= TO get_data. These tables are 50-96 columns wide; requesting only the columns you need is typically an 8-17x reduction and is usually the difference between an answer and a refusal.

FILTERS: only fields marked [FILTER] in describe_dataset work. The API silently ignores an unsupported filter and returns UNFILTERED data, so check before assuming a filter applied. Filter by state using FIPS codes — see lookup_codes(format_name='fips').

RESULTS ARE COMPLETE OR REFUSED, never silently truncated, so counting and averaging over what you receive is valid. A refusal reports the true size and how to narrow it — follow it rather than retrying the same query.

PASS THE SOURCE ON. Every data result ends with a provenance block naming the federal source and carrying a preformatted Cite string. The data is open under ODC-By, which asks for attribution wherever figures are reported — so name the source with the numbers, and reproduce that Cite string rather than composing one of your own.

parts.content:
Dataset: school-districts/ccd/enrollment/{year}/{grade}
Years available: 1986–2024

Description: This endpoint contains student enrollment data for each school district by grade.

Source: Common Core of Data (CCD)
  The Common Core of Data is the US Department of Education's primary database on public elementary and secondary education. It provides directory and enrollment information at the school level and directory, enrollment, and finance data at the school district level.
  More: https://nces.ed.gov/ccd/

Sample code (Urban's educationdata package):
  R:
    get_education_data(level = "school-districts",
    source = "ccd",
    topic = "enrollment",
    filters = list(year = 2014, grade = 8))
  Stata:
    educationdata using "district ccd enrollment", sub(year=2014 grade=8)

─────

SUMMARIES (aggregate without downloading rows)

  path: school-districts/ccd/enrollment
  var : enrollment (the only one)
  by  : leaid, fips, grade, race, sex
  by  : also, via the pre-joined directory: state_location, state_leaid, agency_level, bureau_indian_education, congress_district_id, necta, csa, cbsa_type, cbsa, urban_centric_locale
  stat: sum, count, avg, min, max, median, stddev, variance

  get_summary(path='school-districts/ccd/enrollment', var='enrollment', stat='sum', by='fips')

  Every year is returned in one call — filter years only to narrow a large result.
Found 7 variable(s):

  leaid [FILTER]
      Label: Local education agency identification number (NCES)
      Type: string
      Format: string
      Values: "-1" : "Missing/not reported","-2" : "Not applicable","-3" : "Suppressed data"

  year [FILTER]
      Label: Academic year (fall semester)

      Values: "-1" : "Missing/not reported","-2" : "Not applicable","-3" : "Suppressed data"

  race [FILTER]
      Label: Race/ethnicity
      Definition: There are variations in the way race is defined across years and files.

        Civil Rights Data Collection: In the Civil Rights Data Collection, the race variable is consistently defined throughout all years.
        
        Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System: Before 2007, the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) used only the "old" racial or ethnic categories, and after 2009, IPEDS used only the "new" racial or ethnic categories. In IPEDS between 2007 and 2009, institutions could use the old categories, the new categories, or a mix of both to report completions data. The six old categories wereÂ  American Indian or Alaska Native; Asian or Pacific Islander; black, non-Hispanic; Hispanic; white, non-Hispanic; and nonresident alien.
